nodes.label: Naive Bayes Classifier
nodes.definition: A probabilistic classifier that combines Bayes' theorem with the assumption that features are conditionally independent given the class.

nodes.label: Supervised Classification
nodes.definition: The task of learning from labeled examples to assign a class to a new instance.

nodes.label: Classes and Features
nodes.definition: An instance is represented by features F1 through Fn, and its predicted category is represented by the class variable C.

nodes.label: Conditional Independence Assumption
nodes.definition: Given the class C, the joint distribution of the features factorizes into individual feature distributions, even if the features are dependent overall.

nodes.label: Naive Bayes Probability Model
nodes.definition: The model expresses the class posterior as p(C|F1,...,Fn) = p(C) × ∏i p(Fi|C) / Z.

nodes.label: Bayes' Theorem
nodes.definition: Bayes' theorem computes the posterior using p(C|F) = p(C) × p(F|C) / p(F).

nodes.label: Class Prior
nodes.definition: The prior p(C) expresses how probable a class is before observing an instance's features.

nodes.label: Likelihood
nodes.definition: The likelihood p(F|C) describes how probable the observed features are under a particular class.

nodes.label: Class Posterior
nodes.definition: The posterior p(C|F) expresses the probability of a class after observing the instance's features.

nodes.label: Evidence and Normalization
nodes.definition: The evidence p(F), also denoted Z, normalizes the posterior and is shared by all candidate classes for a fixed instance.

nodes.label: Joint Distribution
nodes.definition: The joint distribution p(C,F1,...,Fn) models the class and features together and equals the numerator in Bayes' theorem.

nodes.label: Probability Chain Rule
nodes.definition: The chain rule expands the joint distribution as p(C) × ∏i p(Fi|C,F1,...,F(i−1)).

nodes.label: Factorized Likelihood
nodes.definition: Conditional independence simplifies the feature likelihood to p(F1,...,Fn|C) = ∏i p(Fi|C).

nodes.label: Maximum A Posteriori Decision
nodes.definition: The MAP rule predicts the class maximizing p(C) × ∏i p(Fi|C), since the evidence is constant across classes.

nodes.label: Parameter Estimation
nodes.definition: Training estimates class priors and the parameters of each class-conditional feature distribution from labeled data.

nodes.label: Maximum Likelihood Estimation
nodes.definition: Maximum likelihood estimation selects model parameters that maximize the likelihood of the observed training data.

nodes.label: Empirical Class Prior
nodes.definition: A class prior can be estimated as the number of training examples in that class divided by the total number of examples.

nodes.label: Uniform Class Prior
nodes.definition: A uniform prior assigns probability 1/K to each of K classes when equal class probabilities are assumed.

nodes.label: Gaussian Naive Bayes
nodes.definition: Gaussian naive Bayes handles continuous features by modeling each feature within each class with a Gaussian distribution.

nodes.label: Class-Conditional Gaussian Density
nodes.definition: For a continuous feature x in class c, its density is p(x|c) = exp(−(x−μc)²/(2σc²)) / √(2πσc²).

nodes.label: Class-Specific Means and Variances
nodes.definition: Gaussian naive Bayes estimates a separate mean and variance for every feature within every class.

nodes.label: Probability Density Versus Probability
nodes.definition: A continuous probability density may exceed one because probabilities are obtained by integrating density over intervals.

nodes.label: Zero-Frequency Problem
nodes.definition: An unseen feature value within a class can receive a zero probability estimate that makes the entire class likelihood zero.

nodes.label: Probability Smoothing
nodes.definition: Smoothing adjusts frequency-based probability estimates so that unseen feature values do not automatically receive zero probability.

nodes.label: Parameter and Training Efficiency
nodes.definition: With a fixed number of parameters per feature and class, factorization makes parameter growth linear in the feature count and avoids estimating a full covariance matrix.

nodes.label: Classification Accuracy Versus Probability Accuracy
nodes.definition: Naive Bayes can classify correctly despite inaccurate probability estimates when the correct class still receives the highest posterior score.

nodes.label: Sex Classification Example
nodes.definition: The resource illustrates Gaussian naive Bayes by predicting a male or female label from height, weight, and foot size.

nodes.label: Training the Measurement Classifier
nodes.definition: Eight labeled examples, four per class, provide class-specific feature means and variances and equal empirical priors of 0.5.

nodes.label: Predicting the Measurement Sample
nodes.definition: The sample with height 6 feet, weight 130 pounds, and foot size 8 inches is assigned female because its unnormalized score is approximately 5.3778×10⁻⁴ versus 6.1984×10⁻⁹ for male.

nodes.label: Text Classification
nodes.definition: Text classification assigns documents to categories using evidence from their words.

nodes.label: Bag-of-Words Representation
nodes.definition: A document is represented by its word occurrences while ignoring their order and positions.

nodes.label: Class-Conditional Word Model
nodes.definition: The text example models document likelihood as p(D|C) = ∏i p(wi|C), multiplying class-conditional probabilities of observed word occurrences.

nodes.label: Spam Filtering
nodes.definition: Spam filtering classifies an email into the mutually exclusive classes spam S and non-spam ¬S.

nodes.label: Posterior Odds
nodes.definition: For spam filtering, posterior odds satisfy p(S|D)/p(¬S|D) = [p(S)/p(¬S)] × ∏i [p(wi|S)/p(wi|¬S)].

nodes.label: Log-Odds Decision Rule
nodes.definition: Taking logarithms gives log posterior odds = log prior odds + ∑i log[p(wi|S)/p(wi|¬S)], with a positive result favoring spam under the MAP rule.
